expression.original: Two element files declaring the same id do not collide; one silently replaces the other in the validated view while the other remains the file a reader sees. verification/python/validate.py:44 keys loaded records by id (out[d.get('id', ...)] = (d, path)); projections/atlas.py:17 appends to a list. Same directory, same glob, different data structure. Adding a file field/elements/zzz-shadow.json carrying id CLM-0003 and altered expression.original produces: 52 files on disk, validate.py reporting elements=51 and CONSISTENT, and — because sorted() order decides — the SHADOW record being the one every consistency condition C1-C12 is evaluated against. field/elements/CLM-0003.json is untouched, shows no diff, and is what a reviewer reads and what git blame reports as unchanged. The candidate change appears in review as a single added file. The validated field and the readable field have come apart with nothing reporting it.
expression.elaboration: This is not a schema gap; every individual record is well-formed. It is a projection failure of the kind CLM-0012 describes, occurring inside the field's own instruments: the dict-keyed load is a many-to-one map whose fiber is never inspected, and the count it prints (len(elements)) is the size of the image, not of the domain. No condition compares files-on-disk to records-loaded, so the difference between 52 and 51 is exactly the information that is discarded. Severity is not theoretical: the mechanism lets an accepted claim's operative content be replaced while its own file's history stays clean, which is the one thing the append-preserving design is meant to make impossible.
expression.unresolved_nuance: Whether the correct repair is to reject duplicate ids outright, or to load by path and treat id collision as a first-class recorded tension, is not decided here. The second preserves more information and matches the field's stated preference for keeping seams open rather than resolving them by fiat. Reopening condition: a proposed condition C13 by an observer other than OBS-AI-0005, together with a negative control that plants a duplicate and shows the alarm ring.
